PLAN "Insulin Sensitivity & Strength — PCOS 12-Week Programme"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "Improve insulin sensitivity via progressive resistance training"
  GOAL secondary body_composition:
    name "Support healthy body composition without caloric restriction stress"
  GOAL tertiary wellbeing:
    name "Reduce overtraining risk; support hormonal regulation"

NUTRITION
  STRATEGY glycaemic_control
  TARGETS
    protein 1.8g_per_kg
    carbohydrate 40_percent_of_calories
    fat 30_percent_of_calories
    fibre 30g_per_day
    hydration 2.5L_per_day
  TIMING
    pre_workout carbohydrate_and_protein within 90 minutes before session
    post_workout protein_and_carbohydrate within 45 minutes after session
    meal_frequency 3_meals_2_snacks_per_day
    avoid_fasting do_not_skip_breakfast
  PRINCIPLES
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise low-GI carbohydrates":
      detail "Choose oats, legumes, sweet potato, quinoa, basmati rice over white bread, white rice, sugary cereals"
    PRINCIPLE "Pair carbohydrates with protein or fat at every meal":
      detail "Blunts postprandial glucose spike; e.g. apple with almond butter, rice with chicken and olive oil"
    PRINCIPLE "Eat protein at breakfast":
      detail "Supports satiety and morning glucose regulation; target 25-35g protein within 1 hour of waking"
    PRINCIPLE "Do not train fasted":
      detail "Under-fuelling elevates cortisol and worsens HPA axis dysregulation common in PCOS; always eat before training"
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise anti-inflammatory fats":
      detail "Oily fish 2-3x per week, extra virgin olive oil, avocado, walnuts; limit saturated fat and avoid trans fats"
    PRINCIPLE "Limit ultra-processed foods and added sugar":
      detail "Target less than 25g added sugar per day; read labels on sauces, yoghurts, and drinks"
    PRINCIPLE "Include inositol-rich foods":
      detail "Citrus fruit, legumes, wholegrains support insulin signalling; discuss myo-inositol supplementation with endocrinologist"
    PRINCIPLE "Manage caffeine timing":
      detail "Caffeine can transiently raise cortisol; limit to 1-2 cups before noon; avoid energy drinks"
    PRINCIPLE "Alcohol minimisation":
      detail "Alcohol disrupts sleep, raises cortisol, and impairs glucose regulation; limit to 1-2 units per week maximum"
  SUPPLEMENTS
    SUPPLEMENT "Vitamin D3 + K2":
      dose "2000-4000 IU D3 daily"
      rationale "Vitamin D deficiency is prevalent in PCOS and impairs insulin signalling; confirm level via GP blood test"
    SUPPLEMENT "Magnesium glycinate":
      dose "300mg elemental magnesium before bed"
      rationale "Supports insulin sensitivity, sleep quality, and reduces cortisol; commonly depleted in PCOS"
    SUPPLEMENT "Omega-3 fish oil":
      dose "2-3g combined EPA+DHA daily with food"
      rationale "Reduces systemic inflammation and supports lipid profile; relevant given HbA1c 5.8"
    SUPPLEMENT "Creatine monohydrate":
      dose "3-5g daily"
      rationale "Supports muscle glucose uptake via GLUT4 upregulation; safe and well-evidenced for females"
  MONITORING
    MONITOR "Weekly fasting glucose proxy":

      detail "Blunts postprandial glucose spike; e.g. apple with almond butter, rice with chicken and olive oil"

      detail "Supports satiety and morning glucose regulation; target 25-35g protein within 1 hour of waking"

    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise anti-inflammatory fats":

    PRINCIPLE "Alcohol minimisation":

      detail "HIIT acutely spikes cortisol; consume 25-30g protein plus 30-40g fast-acting carbohydrate within 30 minutes of finishing any HIIT session to blunt cortisol rebound and support recovery"

      detail "A deficit greater than 300-400 kcal per day is not prescribed for this client. Aggressive restriction in PCOS with HbA1c 5.8 and irregular cycles causes: (1) cortisol elevation that directly worsens insulin resistance, negating the purpose of this programme; (2) suppression of LH and FSH, worsening cycle irregularity or causing amenorrhoea; (3) loss of lean muscle mass, reducing the primary driver of glucose disposal; (4) increased androgen exposure due to stress-driven adrenal activation.     PRINCIPLE "Prioritise low-GI carbohydrates":
      detail "Choose oats, legumes, sweet potato, quinoa, basmati rice over white bread, white rice, sugary cereals"
    PRINCIPLE "Pair carbohydrates with protein or fat at every meal":
      detail "Blunts postprandial glucose spike; e.g. apple with almond butter, rice with chicken and olive oil"
    PRINCIPLE "Eat protein at breakfast":
      detail "Supports satiety and morning glucose regulation; target 25-35g protein within 1 hour of waking"
    PRINCIPLE "Do not train fasted":
      detail "Under-fuelling elevates cortisol and worsens HPA axis dysregulation common in PCOS; always eat before training"
    PRINCIPLE "Prioritise anti-inflammatory fats":
      detail "Oily fish 2-3x per week, extra virgin olive oil, avocado, walnuts; limit saturated fat and avoid trans fats"
    PRINCIPLE "Limit ultra-processed foods and added sugar":
      detail "Target less than 25g added sugar per day; read labels on sauces, yoghurts, and drinks"
    PRINCIPLE "Include inositol-rich foods":
      detail "Citrus fruit, legumes, wholegrains support insulin signalling; discuss myo-inositol supplementation with endocrinologist"
    PRINCIPLE "Manage caffeine timing":
      detail "Caffeine can transiently raise cortisol; limit to 1-2 cups before noon; avoid energy drinks"
    PRINCIPLE "Alcohol minimisation":
      detail "Alcohol disrupts sleep, raises cortisol, and impairs glucose regulation; limit to 1-2 units per week maximum"
    PRINCIPLE "Cardio fuelling — do not use cardio as a reason to under-eat":
      detail "Added cardio increases total energy expenditure; compensate with an additional 20-30g carbohydrate on cardio days to avoid cortisol-driven catabolism and cycle disruption"
    PRINCIPLE "High-intensity training days require more fuel":
      detail "Phase 2 sessions reach RPE 8-9; increase pre-workout carbohydrate to 40-50g and post-workout protein to 35-40g on these days; do not restrict food on hard training days"

      detail "A deficit greater than 300-400 kcal per day is not prescribed for this client. Aggressive restriction in PCOS with HbA1c 5.8 and irregular cycles causes: (1) cortisol elevation that directly worsens insulin resistance, negating the purpose of this programme; (2) suppression of LH and FSH, worsening cycle irregularity or causing amenorrhoea; (3) loss of lean muscle mass, reducing the primary driver of glucose disposal; (4) increased androgen exposure due to stress-driven adrenal activation. A modest deficit of 200-300 kcal below TDEE on rest days only, achieved through food quality improvements rather than restriction, is the maximum safe approach. This must be discussed with the client's endocrinologist before any caloric target is set"
